To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phenol induces membrane changes in free E. coli, and that immobilization of E. coli cells in alginate beads also induces membrane changes.

the presence of phenols in the growth medium induces changes in the lipid composition of the membranes, the protein pattern of E. coli outer membrane and the respiratory activity of its cytoplasmic membranes.
growth of E. coli in the presence of 0.2 M phenol results in reduced lipid-to-proteins ratios of the cytoplASMic and outer membranes and in a decreased amount of proteins in the outer membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of phenol on the structure and the activity of membranes from E. coli.
phenol-induced changes in membrane structure and function of E. coli cells.
the effects of the presence of phenolic compounds on E. coli cells, both in the free form and immobilized in calcium alginate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phenol-induced membrane changes were not only due to the direct interaction with the membranes, but that the growth in the presence of the compound also had an effect on membrane properties.
the presence of phenols in the growth medium induces membrane changes which are different from those caused by the immobilization of cells.

the presence of phenolic compounds in the growth medium of E. coli leads to the induction of membrane proteins involved in the uptake and detoxification of phenols and that the presence of these compounds also leads to a change in membrane fluidity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of phenols during the cultivation of E. coli cells and the entrapment of cells in calcium alginate both induce membrane changes, which may be important for the biodegradability of the immobilized cells.

phenol induces changes in the lipid composition of the membranes and the expression of proteins in the outer membrane of E. coli cells and that immobilization of cells changes the protein expression in the outer membrane.

the presence of phenols in the growth medium induces changes in the lipid-to-protein ratio of the membranes, in the protein composition of the outer membrane and in the respiratory activity of cytoplasmic membranes, but not in the inhibition of O2 uptake by the outer membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phenol-induced membrane changes are different in free and immobilised E. coli cells, which may be of importance when using immobilised cells for the degradation of phenolic compounds.
phenol is a potent inducer of membrane changes in both free and entrapped E. coli, but the effects are not identical in the different cell systems.
phenol is a potent inducer of membrane changes in E. coli.
